subject: Government
title: Principles of Nigeria's Foreign Policy
outline: Meaning of foreign policy and national interest
Basic principles including Africa as centrepiece
Instruments and machinery of foreign policy
Nigeria's foreign policy from 1960 to date

modules.title: Objectives, Principles and Determinants
modules.html:
1. Meaning

Foreign policy is the set of principles, objectives and actions guiding a state's relations with other states and international organisations. It is the projection of national interest — the sum of a state's vital concerns: survival, security, economic wellbeing, prestige and ideological goals — beyond its borders.

2. Objectives (section 19, 1999 Constitution)

  1. Promotion and protection of the national interest.
  2. Promotion of African integration and support for African unity.
  3. Promotion of international cooperation for the consolidation of universal peace and mutual respect among all nations, and elimination of discrimination in all its manifestations.
  4. Respect for international law and treaty obligations, and seeking settlement of disputes by negotiation, mediation, conciliation, arbitration and adjudication.
  5. Promotion of a just world economic order.

3. Basic Principles

  • Africa as the centrepiece of Nigeria's foreign policy.
  • Sovereign equality of all states and respect for their territorial integrity.
  • Non-interference in the internal affairs of other states.
  • Non-alignment with any power bloc.
  • Total eradication of colonialism, apartheid and racial discrimination.
  • Peaceful settlement of disputes and multilateralism through the UN, AU and ECOWAS.
  • Good neighbourliness and economic diplomacy.

4. Determinants

InternalExternal
Size, population and geographyStructure of the international system
Economic and military capabilityInternational law and organisations
Ideology and political systemActions of neighbours and great powers
Leadership and personality of decision-makersWorld public opinion
Public opinion, press and pressure groupsGlobal economic conditions and oil prices
Historical and colonial experienceAlliances and treaty commitments

5. Machinery

The President as chief foreign-policy maker, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, embassies and high commissions, the National Assembly (treaty ratification and budget), the Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (research), Nigerians in Diaspora Commission, and the Technical Aid Corps which posts Nigerian professionals to other developing countries.

examples.q: Explain 'Africa as the centrepiece' with two concrete examples.
examples.a: It means Nigeria treats African liberation, unity and stability as its first external priority. Examples: (i) the establishment of the Southern Africa Relief Fund and material and diplomatic support for liberation movements in Angola, Mozambique, Zimbabwe and South Africa — Nigeria nationalised British Petroleum's interests in 1979 to press Britain over Rhodesia; (ii) leadership and funding of ECOMOG in Liberia (1990) and Sierra Leone (1997–99), where Nigeria supplied most troops and money to restore peace.

examples.q: Why did Nigeria adopt non-alignment at independence?
examples.a: To preserve freedom of action in the Cold War: alignment with either the Western or the Eastern bloc would have subordinated Nigerian decisions to bloc discipline, invited superpower rivalry onto Nigerian soil, and contradicted the anti-colonial stance. Non-alignment allowed Nigeria to trade with and receive aid from both blocs, to judge each issue on its merits, and to build solidarity with other developing states in the Non-Aligned Movement.

modules.title: Nigeria's Foreign Policy in Practice, 1960 to Date
modules.html:
1. Phases

PeriodOrientationHighlights
1960–1966 (Balewa)Cautious, pro-West, legalisticJoined UN and Commonwealth 1960; troops to the Congo (ONUC) 1960; abrogated the Anglo-Nigerian Defence Pact 1962 after student protest; Monrovia group; helped found the OAU 1963
1966–1975 (Gowon)Reconciliation and regionalismCivil-war diplomacy; good neighbourliness; founding of ECOWAS in 1975 with Togo
1975–1979 (Murtala/Obasanjo)Radical and AfrocentricRecognition of the MPLA in Angola against US pressure; 'Africa has come of age' speech; nationalisation of BP assets 1979; FESTAC 1977
1979–1983 (Shagari)Moderate, economic focusExpulsion of illegal aliens 1983; Chad conflict mediation
1985–1993 (Babangida)Economic diplomacyDebt rescheduling; Technical Aid Corps 1987; ECOMOG intervention in Liberia 1990; controversial OIC membership 1986
1993–1998 (Abacha)IsolationCommonwealth suspension after the 1995 execution of Ken Saro-Wiwa; ECOMOG in Sierra Leone
1999–presentShuttle diplomacy and citizen diplomacyRe-admission to the Commonwealth; NEPAD and transformation of the OAU into the AU in 2002; peaceful handover of Bakassi to Cameroon in 2008 after the 2002 ICJ judgment; leadership in ECOWAS responses to coups

2. Achievements

  • Leadership in the OAU/AU and ECOWAS.
  • Peacekeeping in the Congo, Chad, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Sudan, Mali and the Gambia.
  • Sustained contribution to the fall of apartheid.
  • Respect for international adjudication in the Bakassi case.
  • Technical Aid Corps assistance to other developing states.

3. Constraints

  • Mono-product oil economy and revenue volatility.
  • Domestic insecurity, poverty and infrastructural weakness.
  • Frequent changes of regime and policy inconsistency.
  • Poor image abroad from corruption and internet fraud.
  • Rivalry from other regional powers and francophone ties to France.
  • Criticism that huge external spending yields little tangible domestic benefit.

examples.q: Evaluate Nigeria's handling of the Bakassi Peninsula dispute.
examples.a: Cameroon sued Nigeria at the International Court of Justice, which in October 2002 awarded the peninsula to Cameroon. Under the Greentree Agreement (2006) Nigeria withdrew and completed the handover in August 2008. The decision upheld Nigeria's declared principles of respect for international law and peaceful settlement of disputes and avoided war, but it was domestically unpopular for displacing Nigerian inhabitants and surrendering resource-rich territory without a referendum — illustrating the tension between principle and national interest.

examples.q: What is meant by citizen diplomacy?
examples.a: Articulated under Foreign Minister Ojo Maduekwe (2007), it holds that the welfare, dignity and treatment of Nigerian citizens at home and abroad should be the primary measure of foreign policy, rather than costly external commitments. It called for reciprocity in visa and trade matters, protection of Nigerians facing discrimination or deportation, and directing diplomacy toward tangible benefits for ordinary Nigerians.

quiz.q: The centrepiece of Nigeria's foreign policy is:
quiz.solution: Since 1960 Africa has been declared the centrepiece of Nigerian foreign policy.

quiz.q: Foreign policy objectives are stated in which section of the 1999 Constitution?
quiz.solution: Section 19 lists the five foreign-policy objectives of the state.

options: Refusing to join any power bloc
quiz.solution: Non-aligned states avoid Cold War bloc membership while judging issues on merit.

quiz.q: The Anglo-Nigerian Defence Pact was abrogated in:
quiz.solution: Student and nationalist protest forced Balewa to cancel it in 1962.
The Treaty of Lagos established ECOWAS on 28 May 1975.

quiz.q: Nigeria recognised the MPLA government of Angola under:
quiz.solution: Murtala's 1976 OAU speech and recognition of the MPLA marked radical Afrocentrism.

quiz.q: The ICJ awarded Bakassi to Cameroon in:
quiz.solution: The judgment came in October 2002; handover was completed in 2008.

quiz.q: The Technical Aid Corps was established in:
quiz.solution: Created in 1987 to send Nigerian professionals to other developing countries.

quiz.q: Nigeria was suspended from the Commonwealth in 1995 because of:
quiz.solution: The Ogoni executions during the Auckland summit triggered suspension.

quiz.q: Which is an internal determinant of foreign policy?
quiz.solution: Domestic capability determines how far ambitions can be pursued.

quiz.q: Nigeria's peacekeeping force in Liberia from 1990 was:
quiz.solution: The ECOWAS Monitoring Group intervened in the Liberian civil war.

quiz.q: The OAU was transformed into the African Union in:
quiz.solution: The AU was formally launched in Durban in July 2002.
It makes the citizen's interest the yardstick of foreign policy.
Nigeria was admitted on 7 October 1960, days after independence.

quiz.q: A major constraint on Nigeria's foreign policy is:
quiz.solution: Oil price volatility limits sustained external commitments.

quiz.q: Nigeria's first major peacekeeping deployment was to:
quiz.solution: Nigerian troops served in the UN operation in the Congo (ONUC) from 1960.
